page.layout: One column of running text, Latin with a Greek word. Running head at top, page number at top right. Right margin carries printed « line marks and stains, not text. No notes, catchword or signature.

main_text.p: judicationem, Græci ὁρισ-[?]μὸν appellant. Ea constitui-tur ex coniunctione firma-menti, & rationis definitio-ne, hoc modo: cū dicat Ore-stes, se patris ulciscendi cau-sa matrem occidisse, rectúm[?] ne fuerit, a filio sine judicio Clytemnestrā occidi. Ergo hac ratione judicationē invenire convenit. Deinceps controversiarum aliquot exempla subijciemus, si prius satis illorum obiectioni fecerimus, qui disputare poterunt; hanc rationem non jurisconsultorum propriam esse, sed totam ex Rhetorum libris, in quib. tradi hęc præcepta con-fue-

page.notes: Greek word at line 1 "ὁρισ-" / "μὸν" is partly unclear; the first line-end reads as ὁρισ-, copied with [?]. "rectúm" is uncertain: the printed word has a long s with an acute on u. The running head and the page number "iii" are uncertain in the scan and marked [?]. The « marks along the right margin are printed line marks, not transcribed as text. The stains and show-through near the lower right are not transcribed. Spellings as printed: "fe" is read as se, "Græci", "hęc", "præcepta" kept with ligatures; u/v and i/j normalised per rule.
